title: Common Ancestor

story.briefing: Two junctions have both failed. The nearest junction that feeds them both is where the crew should cut power.
story.success: Shared ancestor identified. One cut isolates both faults.

description: A binary search tree holds, at every node, only smaller values in its left subtree and only larger values in its right. All values are distinct. Given such a tree and two values that both appear in it, return the value of the deepest node having both of them somewhere beneath it — counting a node as being beneath itself, so if one value is an ancestor of the other, that value is the answer. A tree is given as an array where the node at index i has its left child at index 2i+1 and its right child at index 2i+2. A null entry means there is no node there, and nothing exists beneath it. An empty array is an empty tree.
constraints: 1 <= tree.length <= 500000, both values are present in the tree

examples.explanation: A node counts as being beneath itself.

hints: While both values are smaller than the current node they are both in its left subtree, so the answer is deeper. The same applies on the right.
The moment the two values fall on opposite sides — or one of them equals the current node — you have gone as deep as you can.
Walk down from the root. Go left while both values are smaller, go right while both are larger, and return the current value as soon as neither is true.
